title: Green's theorem for smooth curves via Mathlib

problemStatement.plain: Formal investigation in analysis: Green's theorem for smooth curves via Mathlib.

currentState.focus: BLOCKED: requires smooth path integral infrastructure not in Mathlib
blockers: Mathlib has no line integral definition for general smooth paths in R^2
No domain integral over bounded regions with smooth boundary
Only circleIntegral exists (complex analysis, not general curves)
Requires 500+ lines: smooth path type, 1-form integration, Stokes machinery

knowledge.progressSummary: BLOCKED: Mathlib has Path x y (continuous) and circleIntegral (complex), but no general smooth path integral or domain integral infrastructure needed for Green on smooth curves.
insights: Mathlib Path type (Topology.Connected.PathConnected) is continuous only — no smoothness
No general line integral of vector fields along parametrized curves in R^2
Parent proof (OQ01) uses intervalIntegral on rectangle boundary — each side is a line segment
Extending to smooth curves needs: (1) smooth path type, (2) line integral def, (3) domain integral, (4) theorem
mathlibGaps: No LineIntegral for vector fields along parametrized smooth curves in R^n
No double integral over bounded domains with smooth boundary (only rectangles via iterated intervalIntegral)
No orientation/winding number machinery for planar curves
nextSteps: Define SmoothPath (Path with C^1 regularity) and LineIntegral for 1-forms
Could state Green for piecewise-smooth curves (sum of integrals over segments)
Intermediate: prove Green for triangular regions (3 segments instead of 4)
Most tractable: define line integral and prove it equals existing rectangular computation for axis-aligned rectangles
